name: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
problem: Colocating prefill and decode in one batch couples their resource-allocation and parallelism plans, so a serving system must trade TTFT against inter-token latency instead of meeting both SLOs.
mechanism: Place prefill workers and decode workers on disjoint GPUs so the two phases cannot preempt each other, then independently choose tensor/pipeline parallelism and worker count per phase to hit a TTFT target and a TPOT target separately. Phase placement is chosen against measured cluster bandwidth to keep the KV handoff cost low. Scheduling uses a parallelism-agnostic goodput-maximising policy that treats each request as a two-stage job.
speedup_reported: Per the OSDI '24 proceedings abstract: 7.4x more requests served OR 12.6x tighter SLO versus state-of-the-art LLM serving systems, while staying within latency constraints for >90% of requests, across popular LLMs, applications and latency requirements. The metric is goodput — the maximum request rate served within BOTH TTFT and TPOT constraints on each GPU. The two figures are alternative operating points, not multiplicative.
